rationale: The single rewrite overloaded one THEN with three separable obligations. (1) two-axis: when sizing or cutting a wagon, assess BOTH footprint (size) and separability (coupling). Complexity is super-linear in cross-wagon coupling. (2) miscut: a wagon that is densely coupled to a neighbor, or contains two internal clusters, is mis-cut even if its footprint is small (MERGE / SPLIT). This part keeps the source patterns and adds no threshold. (3) enforcement-posture: different activation (handling wagon-coupling findings, or designing, implementing or promoting validators, in any phase) and a different reader. no-consume-cycle is the exact invariant. Separability and granularity signals stay advisory until calibrated, and calibration must come before any promotion to strict. Henry-Kafura and treewidth are rationale only, enforced through conservative graph proxies. The source is documentation-only, so no part adds acceptance evidence duties. Evidence items are labelled as nonbinding illustrations. The parts are linked with requires so the assessment, the remedies and the advisory posture travel together. Edges that point at the model (no-consume-cycle, coupling-complexity) are remapped so that they also deliver the model-bearing part.

parts.title: Size a wagon on two axes: footprint and separability

facts.note: Task text is about designing, sizing or recomposing wagons.
The planner authors or changes wagon definitions, including early boundary design.
Artifacts where wagon cuts are designed or declared.
Judged from the task context: is a wagon's boundary or size being decided?

fires: The planner designs or sizes a new wagon.
The planner sizes a wagon and has considered only its footprint.
doesNotFire: Pure footprint scoring of a feature where no wagon boundary is being decided (planner.feature.footprint-scoring alone applies).
Code edits inside a wagon that change neither its WMBTs, its boundary, nor its produce/consume declarations.

parts.given: A wagon is being designed, sized or recomposed.
parts.when: The planner decides the wagon's size and boundary.
parts.then: Size the wagon on two orthogonal axes: SIZE (intrinsic footprint: how much work is inside) and SEPARABILITY (is the wagon a well-separated unit in the produce/consume graph, i.e. is the cut correct?). Treat complexity as super-linear in cross-wagon coupling, not additive in component count.
prefer: Size axis: the additive footprint, sum(count x weight), from planner.feature.footprint-scoring.

Separability axis: a wagon is separable when its cohesion (shared-artifact / object-of-control density of its own WMBTs) is at least its tightest coupling (shared produce/consume artifact-name weight) to any single neighbor wagon.
avoid: Sizing a wagon on footprint alone.
Treating complexity as additive in component count.
parts.why: Complexity is super-linear in cross-wagon coupling, so footprint alone cannot tell you whether a cut is correct.
evidence: Nonbinding illustration (the source is documentation-only; this is not an acceptance requirement): wagon sizing reasoning, where it exists, does not treat a small footprint as proof of a correct cut.
verifier_detail: Terms: size_axis = intrinsic footprint, the additive volume of components (planner.feature.footprint-scoring). separability_axis = coupling complexity, i.e. whether the wagon is a well-separated unit in the produce/consume graph. cohesion = intra-wagon shared-artifact / object-of-control density of a wagon's own WMBTs. coupling = shared produce/consume artifact-name weight between a wagon and a neighbor wagon. separable = internal cohesion is at least the tightest coupling to any single neighbor.
Source disposition: documentation-only, severity 2. This part has no detector of its own and imposes no acceptance evidence.

parts.title: A small wagon can still be mis-cut: MERGE or SPLIT

doesNotFire: Code edits inside a wagon that change neither its WMBTs, its boundary, nor its produce/consume declarations.

parts.given: A wagon cut is being judged.
parts.when: The wagon is densely coupled to a neighbor, or it contains two internal clusters.
parts.then: The wagon can be mis-cut even if its footprint is small. Densely coupled to a neighbor -> MERGE. Two internal clusters -> SPLIT.
prefer: Apply the source's two patterns as stated: densely coupled to a neighbor -> MERGE; two internal clusters -> SPLIT.
avoid: Calling a wagon well-cut just because its footprint is small.
parts.why: Complexity is super-linear in cross-wagon coupling, so a small wagon can still be mis-cut.
evidence: Nonbinding illustration (the source is documentation-only; this is not an acceptance requirement): a wagon's footprint alone is not cited as proof that its cut is correct.
verifier_detail: Mis-cut patterns from the source: densely coupled to a neighbor -> MERGE; two internal clusters -> SPLIT. The source gives no numeric threshold for either pattern.
Signals of these patterns are advisory until calibrated (see planner.wagon.complexity-model.enforcement-posture).

parts.title: no-consume-cycle is the exact invariant; separability and granularity signals stay advisory until calibrated

facts.note: Validator or reporter findings about wagon coupling.
Counts only in a wagon-coupling context.

fires: Someone handles a coupling, separability, granularity or consume-cycle finding.
Someone treats a separability/granularity signal or a MERGE/SPLIT pattern as a blocking gate before calibration.
Someone designs or implements a wagon-coupling validator, or proposes enforcing Henry-Kafura or treewidth metrics.

doesNotFire: Pure footprint scoring with no coupling findings and no validator decisions.

parts.given: A wagon-coupling finding is being handled, or wagon-coupling enforcement is being designed, implemented or promoted.
parts.when: Deciding how binding a wagon-coupling check is.
parts.then: planner.wagon.no-consume-cycle is the first enforcement and the exact invariant. Separability and granularity signals are advisory. Calibrate them before any promotion to strict. Promotion after calibration remains possible.
prefer: Conservative graph proxies: cross-wagon fan-in/fan-out, shared-artifact adjacency, SCCs, community-cut signals.
avoid: Promoting separability or granularity signals to strict without calibrating them first.
Requiring Henry-Kafura (fan_in x fan_out)^2 or treewidth computations as day-one enforcement. They are rationale only.
parts.why: Henry-Kafura and treewidth back the super-linear model conceptually. Enforcement uses conservative proxies so that validators do not become noisy before corpus calibration.
evidence: Nonbinding illustration (the source is documentation-only; this is not an acceptance requirement): any separability or granularity check marked strict has been calibrated first.
verifier_detail: Source disposition: documentation-only, severity 2. The principle has no detector of its own. The exact acyclicity invariant is owned and enforced by planner.wagon.no-consume-cycle. planner.wagon.separability and planner.wagon.coupling-complexity are advisory until calibrated.

Implementation proxies: cross-wagon fan-in/fan-out, shared-artifact adjacency, strongly connected components (SCCs), community-cut signals. Henry-Kafura (fan_in x fan_out)^2 and treewidth are rationale, not day-one enforcement.
